key_insight: Replacing a random latent-to-text mapping with a learned diffusion language model produces lower-perplexity attack prompts while preserving the continuous Gaussian latent-space framework.
engineering_relevance: Black-box LLM risk assessments can depend strongly on prompt generation, with estimated risk differing by an order of magnitude between mappings.
method: Use a continuous diffusion language model to decode standard-Gaussian latents into text.
Preserve downstream sampling and optimization procedures.
Evaluate sampling-based RareTrap and optimization-based ThinkTrap.
evidence_signal: Character-level perplexity falls from 10³–10⁷ to 3–5 in RareTrap and from 20–28 to 4.3–5.4 in ThinkTrap.
watch_item: Lower perplexity does not by itself establish guardrail evasion or representativeness of real-world prompts.
paper_title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
